sentences.zh: 现在，鲁道夫是皇帝唯一的儿子。

sentences.en: Under other circumstances, the crown, the role of the heir apparent, would now have passed to the emperor's brother, Maximilian.
sentences.zh: 在其他情况下，王位和法定继承人的角色本应传给皇帝的弟弟马克西米利安。

sentences.en: But, of course, Maximilian has come to a very sticky end, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，马克西米利安落得个极其悲惨的下场，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, because he's gone off to be emperor in Mexico and been shot.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他去墨西哥当皇帝结果被枪杀了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, actually, the title would now pass to Franz Ferdinand's father, Karl Ludwig.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，这个头衔现在应该传给弗朗茨·斐迪南的父亲卡尔·路德维希。

sentences.en: But, Karl Ludwig is quite old and he's not in terribly good health.
sentences.zh: 但是，卡尔·路德维希年纪已经很大了，而且健康状况不是很好。

sentences.en: So, when Karl Ludwig dies seven years later,
sentences.zh: 因此，当卡尔·路德维希在七年后去世时

sentences.en: Franz Ferdinand, the emperor's nephew, is unexpectedly the heir to the Austrian throne and will inherit the reigns of this extraordinary multinational dynastic empire.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南，作为皇帝的侄子，意外地成为了奥地利王位的继承人，并将继承这个非凡的多元民族王朝帝国的统治权。

sentences.en: Well, the description of it is usually ramshackle.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对它的描述通常是破败不堪的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you think it's ramshackle?
sentences.zh: 你觉得它破败不堪吗？

sentences.en: This is a really thorny kind of historical question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棘手的历史问题。

sentences.en: We know that Austria-Hungary broke up, obviously, at the end of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，显而易见，奥匈帝国在第一次世界大战结束时解体了。

sentences.en: And so, I think, for a long time, there was a lot of back projection.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为，在很长一段时间里，存在着很多事后投射。

sentences.en: And the classic thing that historians would say about it is it's stagnant, it's ramshackle.
sentences.zh: 历史学家对它的经典评价就是：它停滞不前，它破败不堪。

sentences.en: I mean, they always use the word sclerotic and, you know, all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们总是用“硬化的”这个词，你知道的，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: So, Tim Butcher in The Trigger, which we've been citing a lot, he quotes from the Beideker to the Empire of 1905.
sentences.zh: 因此，蒂姆·布彻在他那本我们经常引用的《导火索》一书中，引用了1905年版贝德克尔帝国指南的内容。

sentences.en: And in this, the Beideker points out that in some areas of the Empire, people will drive on the right and some people drive on the left.
sentences.zh: 在这里，贝德克尔指出，在帝国的某些地区，人们靠右行驶，而有些地区人们靠左行驶。

sentences.en: And then Butcher says it did not say what happened when the two driving styles collided.
sentences.zh: 然后布彻说，它没有说明这两种驾驶风格碰撞时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I guess that that is always the risk, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这始终是风险所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: With not just Austria and Hungary, but also all the various constituent parts who are not given equal status with Austria and Hungary, that they all have different interests.
sentences.zh: 不仅是奥地利和匈牙利，还有所有那些没有获得与奥地利和匈牙利同等地位的各个组成部分，它们都有各自不同的利益。

sentences.en: And occasionally, they're going to come into collision with each other.
sentences.zh: 而且偶尔地，它们会彼此发生冲突。

sentences.en: Well, occasionally.
sentences.zh: 嗯，偶尔。

sentences.en: I mean, all the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，无时无刻不在发生。

sentences.en: So, just to give people a sense of some of the nationalities, we're talking about Germans, Czechs, Hungarians, Poles, Ukrainians, Italians,
sentences.zh: 所以，为了让大家对其中的一些民族有个概念，我们说的是德国人、捷克人、匈牙利人、波兰人、乌克兰人、意大利人、

sentences.en: Romanians, Croats, Slovenes, Slovaks, Serbs, and so on, and so on.
sentences.zh: 罗马尼亚人、克罗地亚人、斯洛文尼亚人、斯洛伐克人、塞尔维亚人等等，等等。

sentences.en: We haven't even mentioned Bosnian MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没提到波斯尼亚穆斯林。

sentences.en: Now, the Austrians, I think it's fair to say, were generally the more liberal of the two partners.
sentences.zh: 现在，奥地利人，我认为这样说挺公允的，通常是这两个伙伴中比较开明的一个。

sentences.en: The Hungarians treated their nationalities issue by basically pretending it didn't exist at all.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利人对待其民族问题的方式基本上是假装它根本不存在。

sentences.en: But I don't think it is fair to say that Austria is a basket case or that it is doomed by nationalism.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，把奥地利说成是一团糟或者说它注定会被民族主义毁灭，这并不客观。

sentences.en: First of all, economically, it's actually reasonably successful.
sentences.zh: 首先，在经济上，它其实相当成功。

sentences.en: You've got a big customs union, integrated markets, transport network, factories, all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 你拥有庞大的关税同盟、一体化的市场、交通网络、工厂，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: It's actually booming, isn't it, at this period?
sentences.zh: 在这个时期，它其实正在蓬勃发展，不是吗？

sentences.en: In the years before the First World War, the Austro-Hungarian economy is growing by about 5% a year.
sentences.zh: 在第一次世界大战前的几年里，奥匈帝国的经济每年增长约5%。

sentences.en: My God, Tom.
sentences.zh: 天哪，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, we'd give a lot for that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们愿意为之付出很多。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What would we give for that today?
sentences.zh: 我们今天愿意为之付出什么？

sentences.en: There actually isn't that much political violence.
sentences.zh: 实际上并没有那么多的政治暴力。

sentences.en: There is some, of course, but it's not as bad as the political violence, for example, in Russia.
sentences.zh: 当然有一些，但它没有例如俄罗斯那样的政治暴力那么严重。

sentences.en: And you could argue it's not as bad as the threat of political violence in Ireland, for example.
sentences.zh: 你也可以说它没有像爱尔兰那样的政治暴力威胁那么严重。

sentences.en: Of course, there are a lot of nationalists.
sentences.zh: 当然，有很多民族主义者。

sentences.en: And all these different national groups are demanding more privileges and more airtime, more money, and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有这些不同的民族群体都在要求更多的特权、更多的话语权、更多的资金以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: More patronage.
sentences.zh: 更多的庇护。

sentences.en: But radical nationalists calling for violent separation are actually pretty rare.
sentences.zh: 但呼吁通过暴力分裂的激进民族主义者其实非常罕见。

sentences.en: Even most nationalist politicians recognize they can probably get more by being in the empire and moaning about it than they would by breaking away.
sentences.zh: 甚至大多数民族主义政治家也认识到，通过留在帝国并对此发牢骚，他们可能比通过脱离获得更多好处。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's interesting, definitely, when it collapses, there are then a lot of nationalists who say, oh, we've made a bit of a mistake.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这很有趣，绝对地，当它崩溃时，有很多民族主义者说，哦，我们犯了个小错误。

sentences.en: I mean, particularly by the 30s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特别是在30年代。

sentences.en: By the 30s, of course.
sentences.zh: 到30年代，当然。

sentences.en: They're saying, oh, I wish we were back with the Habsburgs.
sentences.zh: 他们在说，哦，我真希望我们能回到哈布斯堡王朝统治下。

sentences.en: Because, of course, if the Habsburg empire breaks up, it is pretty obvious there will be a lot of fighting about who inherits which bits and where they draw the borders.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，如果哈布斯堡帝国解体，很明显会有一场关于谁继承哪些部分以及在哪里划定边界的大量争斗。

sentences.en: Now, all of that said, of course, it's not perfect.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，当然，它并不完美。

sentences.en: For one thing, the court is incredibly conservative.
sentences.zh: 一方面，宫廷极其保守。

sentences.en: I often wonder whether it's a classic case of kind of overcompensating because they have been on the retreat and because they have lost some of their former power.
sentences.zh: 我常常想，这是否是一个过度补偿的经典案例，因为他们一直在退缩，因为他们失去了部分以往的权力。

sentences.en: And so they're trying much too hard to pretend that nothing has changed.
sentences.zh: 所以他们太努力地假装一切都没有改变。

sentences.en: So, Franz Joseph is pathologically conservative and hierarchical.
sentences.zh: 因此，弗朗茨·约瑟夫病态地保守且等级森严。

sentences.en: You know, we laugh at George V having his strict views about how you creased your trousers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们嘲笑乔治五世对裤子怎么折叠有着严格的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, Franz Joseph, the issue of what trousers you're wearing is an existential one.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对弗朗茨·约瑟夫来说，你穿什么裤子是个生死攸关的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He becomes a very melancholy, sort of pessimistic figure, not least because, I mean, his son has committed suicide.
sentences.zh: 他变成了一个非常忧郁、有点悲观的人物，很大程度上是因为，我的意思是，他的儿子自杀了。

sentences.en: His brother's been shot.
sentences.zh: 他的兄弟被枪杀了。

sentences.en: His brother has been killed in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 他的兄弟在墨西哥被杀害了。

sentences.en: But then his wife, the most glamorous woman in Europe, Cece Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 但随后他的妻子，欧洲最迷人的女性，茜茜，伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: The Diana.
sentences.zh: 戴安娜。

sentences.en: She's the Diana with knobs on of her era.
sentences.zh: 她是他那个时代加剧版的戴安娜。

sentences.en: She was murdered on Lake Geneva by an Italian anarchist in 1898.
sentences.zh: 她在1898年被一名意大利无政府主义者在日内瓦湖畔谋杀。

sentences.en: So, from that point onwards, Franz Joseph becomes very lonely and sad and kind of reclusive.
sentences.zh: 因此，从那时起，弗朗茨·约瑟夫变得非常孤独、悲伤且有些离群索居。

sentences.en: So, Franz Ferdinand grows up in this world.
sentences.zh: 所以，弗朗茨·斐迪南就是在这样一个世界中长大的。

sentences.en: He's in the army, commissioned in the army when he's 12.
sentences.zh: 他在军队里，12岁时就被委任为军队军官。

sentences.en: He basically is steeped in the kind of the world of the Habsburg army, which is, of course, the one institution that's really holding the empire together.
sentences.zh: 他基本上沉浸在哈布斯堡军队的世界里，当然，这是真正维系帝国在一起的唯一机构。

sentences.en: It's also, interestingly, it's an institution where the Austrian side is given a degree of primacy because everyone is expected to speak German, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这也是一个奥地利方面被赋予一定首要地位的机构，因为每个人都被期望说德语，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which the Hungarians don't.
sentences.zh: 而匈牙利人则不然。

sentences.en: And we'll come on to this.
sentences.zh: 我们接下来会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: Franz Ferdinand, the fact that the Hungarians don't speak German is an unbelievable affront.
sentences.zh: 对于弗朗茨·斐迪南来说，匈牙利人不会说德语是一个难以置信的侮辱。

sentences.en: Absolutely intolerable.
sentences.zh: 绝对不可容忍。

sentences.en: So, he, you know, when you look at photos of him as a young man, he's always wearing very tight uniforms, admiring his enormous moustache,
sentences.zh: 所以他，你知道的，当你看着他年轻时的照片时，他总是穿着非常紧身的制服，欣赏着他那巨大的胡子，

sentences.en: sort of sitting around in the office's mess with the other Habsburg officers and things.
sentences.zh: 有点和其他哈布斯堡军官一起坐在军官食堂里之类的。

sentences.en: And that's his milieu.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的圈子。

sentences.en: The problem for him is that the emperor has never recovered from the loss of his son and makes no effort whatsoever to disguise the fact that he considers Franz Ferdinand an absolute waste of space.
sentences.zh: 对他的问题在于，皇帝从未从失去儿子的悲痛中恢复过来，并且毫不掩饰他认为弗朗茨·斐迪南绝对是个废物的态度。

sentences.en: So, when they first met after the Myerling tragedy, the emperor treated Franz Ferdinand really like dirt.
sentences.zh: 因此，在梅耶林悲剧之后他们第一次见面时，皇帝对弗朗茨·斐迪南简直像对待垃圾一样。

sentences.en: Franz Ferdinand said afterwards, I've never been treated so coldly before.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南事后说，我从未受到过如此冷酷的对待。

sentences.en: The mere sight of me seems to awaken unpleasant memories for the emperor.
sentences.zh: 仅仅看到我似乎就会唤起皇帝不愉快的记忆。

sentences.en: It's like Denethor mourning Boromir.
sentences.zh: 这就像德内梭尔哀悼博罗米尔。

sentences.en: It totally is.
sentences.zh: 完全就是这样。

sentences.en: Rejecting Faramir.
sentences.zh: 拒绝法拉米尔。

sentences.en: No, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对是。

sentences.en: There was no warmth between them and never is.
sentences.zh: 他们之间没有任何温暖，也从未有过。

sentences.en: The sad thing is that Franz Ferdinand, he clearly admired Franz Joseph enormously, was very respectful of him, never spoke out of his voice.
sentences.zh: 令人难过的是，弗朗茨·斐迪南显然非常崇拜弗朗茨·约瑟夫，对她非常尊敬，从不在他面前出言不逊。

sentences.en: Out of turn, never criticized him, never betrayed a hint of his frustration.
sentences.zh: 从不出格，从未批评过他，从未流露出一丝沮丧。

sentences.en: And yet, the emperor continued to treat him with sort of cold indifference.
sentences.zh: 然而，皇帝继续以一种冷漠的态度对待他。

sentences.en: And do you think this is why he's so rude to other people?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这就是为什么他对别人那么粗鲁吗？

sentences.en: So kind of short with other people?
sentences.zh: 对别人那么不耐烦？

sentences.en: Franz Ferdinand is famously a very short-tempered man.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南出了名是个脾气暴躁的人。

sentences.en: And clearly, a lot of this is, I think, because he's a very frustrated man.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这其中很大一部分，我认为，是因为他是一个非常沮丧的人。

sentences.en: The round-the-world trip, for example, he's clearly curious.
sentences.zh: 例如，环球旅行，他显然充满了好奇。

sentences.en: When you see those photos of him on the day of the assassination in Sarajevo, where he does, as you put it, he looks like an Austrian walrus.
sentences.zh: 当你看到他在萨拉热窝遇刺那天的那些照片时，正如你所说，他看起来像个奥地利海象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You don't think of him as a sort of curious man, as a stream trying to break its banks.
sentences.zh: 你不会认为他是一个充满好奇心的人，就像一条试图冲破堤岸的河流。

sentences.en: But that's why that photograph of him in the pharaoh's coffin is so unexpected.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么他在法老棺材里的那张照片如此出人意料。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And funny.
sentences.zh: 而且很有趣。

sentences.en: It is funny.
sentences.zh: 确实很有趣。

sentences.en: So he does the round-the-world trip, and he writes that lyrical passage about it, about how much he loved seeing new experiences and learning and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他进行了环球旅行，并为此写了一段抒情的文字，关于他是多么喜欢看到新的经历、学习以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: Then a year later, he fell ill with lung probleMs.
sentences.zh: 然后一年后，他患上了肺部疾病。

sentences.en: He probably had a version of TB.
sentences.zh: 他可能得了某种结核病。

sentences.en: Like Gavrile Princip.
sentences.zh: 就像加夫里洛·普林西普一样。

sentences.en: And he was sent to Egypt to recuperate.
sentences.zh: 他被送到埃及去疗养。

sentences.en: That's when he poses as a mummy.
sentences.zh: 那就是他摆出木乃伊姿势的时候。

sentences.en: But when he's away, everybody thinks he's going to die.
sentences.zh: 但当他不在的时候，大家都以为他要死了。

sentences.en: And they say, oh, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说，哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: His younger brother Otto is the new heir now.
sentences.zh: 他的弟弟奥托现在是新继承人了。

sentences.en: And the emperor and everybody else treats Otto as the heir.
sentences.zh: 皇帝和其他所有人都把奥托当作继承人对待。

sentences.en: And Franz Ferdinand knows this, and he's absolutely gutted.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南知道这一点，他感到无比痛心。

sentences.en: And so when he comes back, and everybody's like, oh, no, he's still alive.
sentences.zh: 所以当他回来时，大家都是一副“哦，不，他还活着”的表情。

sentences.en: He's really hurt, I think, and disappointed by this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让他感到非常受伤和失望。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, almost any account you read of him says, you know, he grew into a man suspicious, morose, and violent, seeing enemies everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，几乎你读到的关于他的任何记述都说，你知道的，他成长为一个多疑、阴郁、暴戾、视敌人无处不在的人。

sentences.en: And because of this, turning would-be friends into enemies.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他把本该成为朋友的人变成了敌人。

sentences.en: He also has the same, I mean, to his credit, Tom, he has the same view of the human condition as I do.
sentences.zh: 值得一提的是，汤姆，他对人类境况的看法跟我一样。

sentences.en: Yes, I saw this.
sentences.zh: 是的，我看到了这一点。

sentences.en: So, I always assume that everyone I meet is a rogue until the contrary is proved.
sentences.zh: 所以，我总是假设我遇到的每个人都是恶棍，直到证明并非如此。

sentences.en: That's exactly what I think.
sentences.zh: 这正是我所想的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely what I think.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全是我所想的。

sentences.en: Incredible.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: So, we've already had Captain Benteen as a kind of analogue to you from 19th century history.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们之前已经有了本廷上尉作为19世纪历史中你的某种对应人物。

sentences.en: And now we've got Franz Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了弗朗茨·斐迪南。

sentences.en: My dream dinner party is Captain Benteen and Franz Ferdinand, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我梦想的晚宴嘉宾是本廷上尉和弗朗茨·斐迪南，汤姆。

sentences.en: No question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: He's very hot-tempered.
sentences.zh: 他脾气非常暴躁。

sentences.en: He's exceptionally rude.
sentences.zh: 他极其粗鲁。

sentences.en: Something else I admire in a...
sentences.zh: 这也是我欣赏的另一点……

sentences.en: So, he's rude to servants.
sentences.zh: 所以，他对仆人很粗鲁。

sentences.en: I don't approve of that, Tom, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 说实话，汤姆，我不赞成那样。

sentences.en: I'm very polite to our servants.
sentences.zh: 我对我们的仆人非常有礼貌。

sentences.en: So, when it comes to birds, I mean, he's terrible to birds, isn't he?

sentences.en: if he had survived to become emperor,
sentences.zh: 如果他活下来并成为皇帝，

sentences.en: So it's not impossible to imagine a Habsburg empire that is not involved in war, continuing, maybe it loses bits.

sentences.en: But it just, it heightens the sense of jeopardy, doesn't it?

sentences.zh: 如果我们把弗朗茨·斐迪南视为一个严肃的改革家。

sentences.zh: 他毫无疑问就是这样的人。

sentences.en: It's obvious Franz Josef is not going to live forever, and that he, Franz Ferdinand, will take over.

sentences.en: So there's a guy called Georg Ritter von Schönerer, who's the guy who invented the Hitler salute,

sentences.zh: 所以他在说，我们需要向新教的德国靠拢。

sentences.zh: 你知道，德国人的德国，一个更大的日耳曼世界。

sentences.zh: 所有这些事情。

sentences.zh: 现在，匈牙利人是实现这一目标的巨大障碍，因为在帝国的匈牙利半边，他们基本上根本不给少数族裔留一点生存空间。

sentences.zh: 他们没有投票权。

sentences.zh: 他们的政治表达非常有限。

sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南认为匈牙利人基本上是巨大的绊脚石。

sentences.zh: 而且他极其鄙视他们。

sentences.zh: 事实上，我一次又一次地回到这个信念上来，我将在有生之年一直表达下去：那个所谓的正派匈牙利人根本不存在。

sentences.en: And that every Hungarian, be he a minister, a prince, a cardinal, a tradesman, a peasant, a hussar, or a stable boy, is a revolutionary and a...
sentences.zh: 每一个匈牙利人，无论是大臣、亲王、红衣主教、商人、农民、骠骑兵还是马夫，都是一个革命者和一个……

sentences.en: And then he just drew a kind of line.
sentences.zh: 然后他只是画了一条线之类的。

sentences.zh: 所以你可以用你自己的话来想象他在想什么词。

sentences.en: So, yeah, he absolutely despises them.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他绝对鄙视他们。

sentences.zh: 为了打破他们的权力，他想出了两个计划。

sentences.zh: 我们在加夫里洛·普林西普的单集里提到过它们。

sentences.en: So the Slav bits, particularly kind of Croatia, Bosnia, the Dalmatian coast, they will be a kingdom of their own, no longer under the thumb of the Austrians or the Hungarians.
sentences.zh: 因此斯拉夫部分，主要是克罗地亚、波斯尼亚、达尔马提亚海岸，将拥有他们自己的王国，不再受奥地利人或匈牙利人的控制。

sentences.en: And this is the thing that is so terrifying for Serbian nationalists.

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there'd be 16 states.
sentences.zh: 所以将会有16个州。

sentences.zh: 会有奥地利、一个小匈牙利、西里西亚、波希米亚、西加利西亚、斯洛文尼亚、特兰西瓦尼亚等等等等。

sentences.zh: 你可以看出那是如何运作的，如何……

sentences.zh: 那么，他能实现这一点吗？

sentences.en: Of course, that was a brilliant way of breaking the power of the Hungarian gentry who are his opponents.

sentences.zh: 所以这会包括罗马尼亚人……

sentences.zh: 所以他是一个不可思议的扩大选举权的爱好者，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 他的另一件大事，我们在前半部分简要谈过，是他对匈牙利人希望在他们那部分的军队中使用自己的语言感到愤怒。

sentences.zh: 所以他一直在为这个语言问题与匈牙利人争斗。

sentences.zh: 然而讽刺的是，弗朗茨·斐迪南唯一永远不想做的事，就是动用那支军队。

sentences.zh: 特别是其中某个人，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 而且是索菲的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: And a big fan of Sophie.
sentences.zh: 而且是索菲的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: So for those listeners who are inclined to look poorly on the Kaiser, because I mean, let's be honest, the Kaiser is a complicated man.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些倾向于看不起德皇的听众来说，因为说实话，德皇是个复杂的人。

sentences.zh: 那么，我是否应该读一下一位顶级历史学家对弗朗茨·斐迪南和德皇之间这种关系的描述？

sentences.en: The two men loved going hunting together and looked forward to the day when they would be empress together, swaggering around with their huge moustaches and ridiculous hats.
sentences.zh: 这两个人喜欢一起去打猎，并期待着有一天他们能一起成为皇帝，留着巨大的胡子，戴着可笑的帽子大摇大摆。

sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 而那顶尖历史学家，多米尼克，就是你自己。

sentences.zh: 是的，在《时间历险：第一次世界大战》中。

sentences.en: So they would meet up and they would wear hunting gear and, you know, compliment each other on their massive moustaches.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会见面，穿着猎装，你知道的，互相夸奖对方硕大的胡子。

sentences.en: And they would go and shoot some birds.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会去射杀一些鸟。

sentences.en: And then the Kaiser would come back and he would be really nice.
sentences.zh: 接着德皇回来后会变得非常好。

sentences.en: He would make a point of being nice to Sophie.
sentences.zh: 他会特意对索菲很好。

sentences.en: So when they went to Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们去德国的时候。

sentences.en: He goes up in my estimation.
sentences.zh: 我对他的评价上升了。

sentences.en: I feel sorry for Sophie.
sentences.zh: 我为索菲感到遗憾。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The Kaiser would say, come and sit by me, Sophie.
sentences.zh: 德皇会说，来坐在我旁边，索菲。

sentences.en: You know, be really kind to her.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，对她真的很好。

sentences.en: All this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: He wrote letters all the time to Franz Ferdinand saying, you know, don't feel stressed about when you're emperor.
sentences.zh: 他一直给弗朗茨·斐迪南写信说，你知道的，当你成为皇帝时不要感到压力。

sentences.en: It'll be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这会很棒的。

sentences.en: We'll have a great time.
sentences.zh: 我们会玩得很开心。

sentences.en: I will be your friend.
sentences.zh: 我会成为你的朋友。

sentences.en: I will always stand by Austria.
sentences.zh: 我将永远支持奥地利。

sentences.en: All of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情。

sentences.en: It sounds flippant.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很轻浮。

sentences.en: But Franz Ferdinand is quite a lonely man.
sentences.zh: 但弗朗茨·斐迪南是个相当孤独的人。

sentences.en: Ostracized by the rest of the family and by the court.
sentences.zh: 被家族其他成员和宫廷所排挤。

sentences.en: The Kaiser's friendship means a lot to him.
sentences.zh: 德皇的友谊对意义重大。

sentences.en: And he will often say to the Kaiser, you know, give me a hand here.
sentences.zh: 而且他经常对德皇说，你知道的，帮我一把。

sentences.en: People are talking of war.
sentences.zh: 人们都在谈论战争。

sentences.en: The Hungarians have been difficult.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利人一直很难对付。

sentences.en: You know, use a bit of your influence if you can.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果可以的话，动用一点你的影响力。

sentences.en: And the Kaiser usually says, you know, I'll do what I can.
sentences.zh: 德皇通常会说，你知道的，我会尽力而为。

sentences.en: And is it right that the particular moment of crisis is in the wake of these two wars, these two Balkan wars,
sentences.zh: 那么，这场危机的特定时刻确实是在这两场战争、这两次巴尔干战争之后吗？

sentences.en: when Serbia has kind of expanded by something like over 80% of its territory?
sentences.zh: 当时塞尔维亚的领土差不多扩张了80%以上？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So the first Balkan war, as we said, October to May 1912, 1913, it's everybody basically ganging up on the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 所以第一次巴尔干战争，正如我们所说，从1912年10月到1913年5月，基本上是所有人都在围攻奥斯曼帝国。

sentences.en: Conrad says again and again, let's attack Serbia now.
sentences.zh: 康拉德一次又一次地说，我们现在就进攻塞尔维亚吧。

sentences.en: Franz Ferdinand is appalled at this.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南对此感到震惊。

sentences.en: Let's not stoop to this hooligism.
sentences.zh: 我们不要沦落到这种无赖行径。

sentences.zh: 我们保持超然，看着这群人狗咬狗、打得头破血流吧。

sentences.en: So he doesn't hold the Serbs and their antagonists in tremendous regard.
sentences.zh: 因此，他对塞尔维亚人及其对头并没有给予极高的评价。

sentences.en: He actually gives a public toast to peace.
sentences.zh: 他甚至公开为和平祝酒。

sentences.en: What would we get out of war with Serbia?
sentences.zh: 跟塞尔维亚打仗我们能得到什么？

sentences.en: All we'd get from beating Serbia.
sentences.zh: 我们打败塞尔维亚能得到的全部东西。

sentences.en: So how do the Serbs misread him so badly?
sentences.zh: 那么塞尔维亚人怎么会对他有如此严重的误解呢？

sentences.en: Because I think they're projecting onto him a stereotype of Austria that is an anchor of their ideology.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为他们把对奥地利的刻板印象投射到了他身上，而这正是他们意识形态的支柱。

sentences.en: Their ideology is Austria is a bullying oppressor.
sentences.zh: 他们的意识形态是奥地利是一个飞扬跋扈的压迫者。

sentences.en: Franz Ferdinand has a gigantic moustache and shooting loads of birds.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南留着巨大的胡子，还射杀大量的鸟类。

sentences.en: Ergo, he is also a bullying oppressor.
sentences.zh: 所以，他也是一个飞扬跋扈的压迫者。

sentences.en: And it doesn't fit in their demonology.
sentences.zh: 这与他们的妖魔化形象不符。

sentences.en: If he's actually a sort of peace figure.
sentences.zh: 如果他实际上是一个某种程度上的和平象征。

sentences.en: But then, as you say, in the Second Balkan War, where everybody ganged up on Bulgaria, the Serbs conquered a lot more of the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，在第二次巴尔干战争中，所有人都在围攻保加利亚，塞尔维亚人征服了巴尔干地区的更多领土。

sentences.en: And reports are going back to Vienna.
sentences.zh: 报告源源不断地传回维也纳。

sentences.en: We have them.
sentences.zh: 我们掌握了这些报告。

sentences.en: We know them.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它们。

sentences.en: They're there in the archives from Austrian consuls in the southern Balkans saying, there are horrendous massacres.
sentences.zh: 它们就在档案里，来自奥地利驻巴尔干南部领事的报告说，那里发生了可怕的大屠杀。

sentences.en: There's horrendous ethnic cleansing going on.
sentences.zh: 那里正在发生可怕的种族清洗。

sentences.en: Entire villages of Albanians or of people who describe themselves as Turks or Muslims wiped out by Serbian paramilitaries.
sentences.zh: 成片的阿尔巴尼亚人村庄，或者自称为土耳其人或穆斯林的村庄，被塞尔维亚准军事部队消灭了。

sentences.en: So the Austrians think, oh, the Serbians are very bad guys.
sentences.zh: 所以奥地利人认为，哦，塞尔维亚人真是坏蛋。

sentences.en: And yet again, Franz Ferdinand says, no, we're not going to get involved.
sentences.zh: 然而弗朗茨·斐迪南又一次说，不，我们不会卷入其中。

sentences.en: It would be the end of the empire if we ever fought a war with Serbia, because it would mean war with Russia.
sentences.zh: 如果我们与塞尔维亚开战，那将是帝国的终结，因为这意味着要与俄罗斯开战。

sentences.en: A war with Russia, he writes at one point, will finish us.
sentences.zh: 他有一次写道，与俄罗斯的战争将彻底毁了我们。

sentences.en: Should the Kaiser of Austria, the Emperor of Austria and the Tsar, knock each other off their thrones and clear the way for revolution?
sentences.zh: 难道奥地利德皇、奥地利皇帝和沙皇要把彼此从王位上拉下来，为革命扫清道路吗？

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 绝不可能。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very prescient, actually.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其实非常有远见。

sentences.en: It's amazingly prescient.
sentences.zh: 真是惊人的有远见。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And just, again, it kind of ratches up the sense of tragedy, really.
sentences.zh: 而且，这再次加剧了一种悲剧感。

sentences.en: That this is the man whose death will ultimately result in precisely those results.
sentences.zh: 这个人，他的死最终将导致恰恰那样的结果。

sentences.en: So when that crisis is over in the autumn of 1913, the Austrians have not gone involved.
sentences.zh: 所以在1913年秋天这场危机结束后，奥地利人并没有卷入其中。

sentences.en: The Balkan Wars, it seems, have ended.
sentences.zh: 巴尔干战争似乎已经结束了。

sentences.zh: 德皇来到了科诺皮斯特。

sentences.en: They have an absolutely brilliant time.
sentences.zh: 他们度过了一段绝对美妙的时光。

sentences.zh: 他们射杀了1100只野鸡。

sentences.en: There's some great banter, Tom, about St. George, who we've just done a podcast on.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，关于圣乔治有一些很棒的玩笑，我们刚刚做过关于他的播客。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You'll enjoy this.
sentences.zh: 你会喜欢这个的。

sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南的爱好之一是收集圣乔治与恶龙的图片。

sentences.en: Yeah, I should have put this in the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，我本该把这个放进播客里的。

sentences.zh: 他有3750幅不同的圣乔治与恶龙的画像。

sentences.zh: 他把这些展示给德皇看。

sentences.zh: 他说，看看你，把时间浪费在和英国人进行无畏舰海军军备竞赛上。

sentences.en: I've already beaten the British.
sentences.zh: 我已经击败英国人了。

sentences.en: I have more images of their patron saint than they have in Windsor Castle.
sentences.zh: 我拥有的他们守护神的画像比他们在温莎城堡里还要多。

sentences.en: And the Kaiser thinks this is absolutely tremendous.
sentences.zh: 德皇觉得这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh, oh, oh, oh, I am liking that very much.
sentences.zh: 哦，哦，哦，哦，哦，哦，哦，哦，我非常喜欢这个。

sentences.en: But actually, actually, Franz Ferdinand, I mean, he's quite keen on Britain, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，实际上，弗朗茨·斐迪南，我的意思是，他对英国挺感兴趣的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I was so shocked at that impression time I nearly fainted.
sentences.zh: 我当时对那个印象震惊得差点昏过去。

sentences.en: He actually had been very down on Britain about 10 or 20 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 大约在10到20年前，他其实对英国非常反感。

sentences.en: But by this point, he's actually, you know, he doesn't mind it.
sentences.zh: 但到了这个时候，实际上，你知道的，他并不介意。

sentences.en: Not least because they are also really into shooting birds.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为他们也真的很喜欢射鸟。

sentences.en: We're a patriotic podcast, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个爱国的播客，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 我必须说，乔治五世和他的宫廷对接下来发生的事情处理得非常好。

sentences.en: Because they also invite Sophie and Franz Ferdinand over to Windsor for a week.
sentences.zh: 因为他们还邀请了索菲和弗朗茨·斐迪南去温莎呆了一个星期。

sentences.en: And this is great for Sophie.
sentences.zh: 这对索菲来说太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a big deal for Franz Ferdinand and Sophie to go to what is considered the kind of premier court in Europe and to be treated as equals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于弗朗茨·斐迪南和索菲来说，去往被认为是欧洲首屈一指的宫廷并被当作平等对待，这是一件大事。

sentences.zh: 星期二我们打了一千多只野鸡，星期三打落450只鸭子。

sentences.zh: 我喜欢星期五的记录，糟糕的一天，狂风暴雨，下午简直是一场大洪水。

sentences.zh: 多么杰出的人啊。

sentences.en: Because no one is a better killer of birth than the Archduke.

sentences.zh: 波特兰公爵，他证明了自己是一流的。

sentences.zh: 他与我任何朋友相比都不逊色。

sentences.zh: 只要有足够的练习，他将不逊色于国内任何顶级神枪手。

sentences.en: High praise.
sentences.zh: 极高的评价。

sentences.en: So everyone says it's great.
sentences.zh: 所以大家都说这很好。

sentences.en: At dinner, Tom, do you know who they sit him opposite?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在晚宴上，你知道他们把他安排坐在谁对面吗？

sentences.en: Your friend, top fisherman, Sir Edward Gray, British Foreign Secretary.
sentences.zh: 你的朋友，顶级渔夫，英国外交大臣爱德华·格雷爵士。

sentences.en: And they talk about world peace.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论世界和平。

sentences.en: Serbia, Albania, they go into all the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚、阿尔巴尼亚，他们深入讨论了巴尔干半岛的所有问题。

sentences.en: And Sir Edward Gray, and everyone says, oh, what a tremendous man the Archduke is.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·格雷爵士，每个人都说，大公真是一个了不起的人啊。

sentences.en: Queen Mary, the Archduke is most amiable.
sentences.zh: 玛丽王后说，大公非常和蔼可亲。

sentences.en: He's making an excellent impression.
sentences.zh: 他留下了极好的印象。

sentences.en: His wife is so nice, agreeable, and easy to get on with.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子是如此善良、讨人喜欢且易于相处。

sentences.en: Very tactful.
sentences.zh: 非常得体。

sentences.zh: 而且事实上，事后她对某人说，他以前很不英国化，但她对他的影响太好了。

sentences.en: They're lovely people.
sentences.zh: 他们都是可爱的人。

sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.zh: 所以他回到了奥地利。

sentences.zh: 他对自己的表现非常满意。

sentences.en: All good.

sentences.zh: 和家人一起过圣诞节。

sentences.zh: 所以这是1913年？

sentences.zh: 如果你能在6月底去波斯尼亚观看我们的军事演习，那就太好了。

sentences.zh: 顺便对萨拉热窝进行一次小访问。

sentences.zh: 树立旗帜。

sentences.en: All of this.

sentences.zh: 问题是，这又是一个我认为很多人忽略的细节。

sentences.zh: 人们说，哦，他真的很想去，因为他和索菲可以聚在一起，诸如此类。

sentences.zh: 他非常担心炎热的天气。

sentences.zh: 而且他知道，他们所有人都知道，存在安全风险。

sentences.zh: 这其实并不是真的。

sentences.zh: 但弗朗茨·斐迪南不是傻子。

sentences.zh: 皇帝破例说，好吧，如果你非要带上你该死的妻子的话。

sentences.en: So he's going to go.
sentences.zh: 所以他还是要去了。

sentences.en: The next day, of course, is the day that there is that sort of coded warning from the ambassador to the finance minister.

sentences.zh: 所以计划是安保工作会非常少，因为重点是要表明我们根本不需要它。

sentences.en: No, it's a normality.
sentences.zh: 不，这很正常。

sentences.zh: 那我们来进入倒计时吧。

sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南在7号星期天前往维也纳德比。

sentences.en: That's all great.
sentences.zh: 这当然很好。

sentences.en: Everyone makes a fuss of him and Sophie.
sentences.zh: 所有人都对他和苏菲大惊小怪。

sentences.en: And in fact, in the next day's papers, lots of people comment about how she's the best dressed and she looks great.
sentences.zh: 事实上，第二天报纸上很多人评论说她穿着最好，看起来棒极了。

sentences.en: And he's very pleased with that.
sentences.zh: 对此他非常高兴。

sentences.en: Back to look at the roses.

sentences.zh: 他们聊了聊改革计划。

sentences.en: Fran Ferdinand says to the Kaiser, I would like you to help me with the Hungarians.
sentences.zh: 弗朗茨·斐迪南对凯撒说，我希望你能在匈牙利人方面帮帮我。

sentences.en: You know, get them to give more concessions to their peasants and the Slavs and stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，让他们对农民和斯拉夫人等给予更多妥协。

sentences.en: And he says it's really crucial to do this.
sentences.zh: 他说这样做真的至关重要。

sentences.en: He's no fool, Fran Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 他可不傻，弗朗茨·斐迪南。

sentences.en: He says that Romanian minority is really important because Romania is moving away from us and towards
sentences.zh: 他说罗马尼亚少数群体真的很重要，因为罗马尼亚正在疏远我们并转向

sentences.zh: 俄罗斯。

sentences.en: We can't afford to alienate the Romanians.
sentences.zh: 我们可承担不起疏远罗马尼亚人的代价。

sentences.en: Therefore, we should really be thinking about what's going on in Hungary and having reforms and keeping them on side.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们真的应该考虑匈牙利正在发生的事情，进行改革并把他们拉拢过来。

sentences.en: And actually, the Kaiser says, you know, I'll do my bit.
sentences.zh: 事实上，凯撒说，你知道的，我会尽我所能。

sentences.en: Don't worry, you can rely on me.
sentences.zh: 别担心，你可以信赖我。

sentences.en: And the visit is such a success that Fran Ferdinand says, this has been brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这次访问太成功了，以至于弗朗茨·斐迪南说，这太棒了。

sentences.en: An absolutely brilliant weekend.
sentences.zh: 一个绝对精彩的周末。

sentences.zh: 我是说，这其实是我梦寐以求的晚宴阵容。

sentences.en: I imagine Sophie's lovely.
sentences.zh: 我想象苏菲一定很可爱。

sentences.en: A big deal for Fran Ferdinand this.

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Lovely to children, I imagine.
sentences.zh: 我想我对小孩子应该挺亲切的。

sentences.en: I think actually they're quite reclusive.
sentences.zh: 其实我觉得他们挺孤僻的。

sentences.en: They don't really mingle much because they're kind of shy.
sentences.zh: 他们其实不太跟人交往，因为他们有点害羞。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.zh: 在这方面我得让你失望了。

sentences.zh: 所以他们去了他们的避暑城堡，一个叫做克鲁姆的地方，位于现在的

sentences.zh: 他们在树林里进行长途散步。

sentences.zh: 他们将分开走。

sentences.zh: 其余的路程则乘坐火车。

sentences.zh: 当他坐火车从维也纳到里雅斯特时发生了一件奇怪的事。

sentences.zh: 火车上发生了电路故障，车厢变得非常热，因为显然没有风扇，而且他们只能靠蜡烛照明。

sentences.en: And Franz Ferdinand says to his kind of chamberlain, see, this is how it's going to start, he says.

sentences.zh: 首先是过热的车厢，然后可能就会有人试图在萨拉热窝枪杀我

sentences.zh: 你知道，他开了个这样的玩笑。
